commit.subject: Validate number of operands for if and switch.
commit.message:
Validate number of operands for if and switch.

Instead of validating the specific operand for the `if` and `switch`
instructions validate that there is only 1 instruction that it is valid.
Fixes an issue where we can accidentally set multiple operands into an
`if` where the operand is actually invalid.

Fixed: 442245491
Change-Id: Ib8d9a5dd35535e55bbe76f4a55737721b59c3805

commit.subject: Store allowNonUniformDerivatives state in ShaderModule.
commit.message:
Store allowNonUniformDerivatives state in ShaderModule.

ShaderModuleBase occasionally needs to reconstruct the descriptor to
recreate tint programs that have been released.
allowNonUniformDerivatives in DawnShaderModuleSPIRVOptionsDescriptor was
not stored or hashed into the ShaderModule's content hash.

Change-Id: I92ef904366d7b8d5480e7cbbb4d1c702b163cb72

commit.subject: Reland "Move FencedDeleter Tick into a SerialTask"
commit.message:
Reland "Move FencedDeleter Tick into a SerialTask"

This is a reland of commit a3335349674d8e6538e35ae0f43ed84767b9f539

Original change's description:
> Move FencedDeleter Tick into a SerialTask
>
> Moves all of the deletions done by FencedDeleter into a SerialTask,
> rather than requiring that Tick be called manually. Tasks are scheduled
> when DeleteWhenUnused is called.
>
> To prevent an excessive amount of tasks from being created and to
> preserve deletion ordering for dependent resources (such as Swapchains
> and Surfaces) all deletions sharing a serial will share a task.
>
> Bug: 430452846
> Change-Id: Ie26bfad14087430f53e73f5c41a3897eb9f1e403
> Reviewed-on: https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/252314
> Reviewed-by: Loko Kung <lokokung@google.com>
> Commit-Queue: Brandon Jones <bajones@chromium.org>

Bug: 430452846
Change-Id: Iba9de33b22fbbf50373f605eb61d2d62928c375a

commit.subject: Cleanup of various lint issues across the code base
commit.message:
Cleanup of various lint issues across the code base

Fixing a variety of issues discovered by running staticcheck locally,
along with other linting issues found via golangci-lint in my IDE.

This does NOT eliminate all of the findings that staticcheck has in
its default configuration, just significantly reduces them. Some
issues require more extensive changes/investigation than I was willing
to put into this CL, or probably should just be suppressed since it is
unlikely we will fix them.

Types of issues identified by staticcheck and fixed:
- should use fmt.Errorf(...) instead of errors.New(fmt.Sprintf(...)) (S1028)
- var <name> is unused (U1000)
- func <name> is unused (U1000)
- type <name> is unused (U1000)
- this value of err is never used (SA4006)
- package <name> is being imported more than once (ST1019)
- unnecessary assignment to the blank identifier (S1005)
- Various "io/ioutil" has been deprecated since Go 1.19
- reflect.PtrTo has been deprecated since Go 1.22
- should use time.Since instead of time.Now().Sub (S1012)
- should use copy(to, from) instead of a loop (S1001)

Other types of issues fixed:
- Various pkg/var name collisions ('auth', 'git', 'gerrit', etc)
- Various direct comparison against errors instead of using errors.Is()
- Redundant conversions, e.g. string("literal")
- Struct <name> has methods on both value and pointer receivers,
  i.e. mixing (c Cmd) and (c *Cmd), there seemed to be lots of false
  positives for this, not clear why
- Ineffectual assignments, e.g. val := "", then immediately assigning
  to val, sometimes these assignments hid unused variables
- Instances where types could be omitted
- Snake case naming

I intentionally did not fix the following findings:
- error strings should not be capitalized (ST1005), since a lot of the
  existing tests are doing string comparison for error checking, so
  would need to be updated also
- strings.Title being deprecated, since it requires a new library call
  to fix, which has different semantics
- Fixing slices being initialized with empty literal instead of nil,
  e.g. var := []int{}. Technically nil for a slice can be appended to
  like an empty slice and some other usages and potentially save an
  allocation if not used, but in other cases, like working with JSON
  marshaling/unmarshaling nil vs an empty slice have semantic
  differences. I think the nil-behaviour of slices was a mistake,
  since it is a bit of a gotcha and really only exists for a niche
  optimization.
- Unused params, which could be fixed via '_'. There are hundreds of
  these in the code base and it is debatable if they should be fixed.
- Warnings about documentation, broadly ignored, since often they were

commit.message:
Cleanup of various lint issues across the code base

Fixing a variety of issues discovered by running staticcheck locally,
along with other linting issues found via golangci-lint in my IDE.

This does NOT eliminate all of the findings that staticcheck has in
its default configuration, just significantly reduces them. Some
issues require more extensive changes/investigation than I was willing
to put into this CL, or probably should just be suppressed since it is
unlikely we will fix them.

Types of issues identified by staticcheck and fixed:
- should use fmt.Errorf(...) instead of errors.New(fmt.Sprintf(...)) (S1028)
- var <name> is unused (U1000)
- func <name> is unused (U1000)
- type <name> is unused (U1000)
- this value of err is never used (SA4006)
- package <name> is being imported more than once (ST1019)
- unnecessary assignment to the blank identifier (S1005)
- Various "io/ioutil" has been deprecated since Go 1.19
- reflect.PtrTo has been deprecated since Go 1.22
- should use time.Since instead of time.Now().Sub (S1012)
- should use copy(to, from) instead of a loop (S1001)

Other types of issues fixed:
- Various pkg/var name collisions ('auth', 'git', 'gerrit', etc)
- Various direct comparison against errors instead of using errors.Is()
- Redundant conversions, e.g. string("literal")
- Struct <name> has methods on both value and pointer receivers,
  i.e. mixing (c Cmd) and (c *Cmd), there seemed to be lots of false
  positives for this, not clear why
- Ineffectual assignments, e.g. val := "", then immediately assigning
  to val, sometimes these assignments hid unused variables
- Instances where types could be omitted
- Snake case naming

I intentionally did not fix the following findings:
- error strings should not be capitalized (ST1005), since a lot of the
  existing tests are doing string comparison for error checking, so
  would need to be updated also
- strings.Title being deprecated, since it requires a new library call
  to fix, which has different semantics
- Fixing slices being initialized with empty literal instead of nil,
  e.g. var := []int{}. Technically nil for a slice can be appended to
  like an empty slice and some other usages and potentially save an
  allocation if not used, but in other cases, like working with JSON
  marshaling/unmarshaling nil vs an empty slice have semantic
  differences. I think the nil-behaviour of slices was a mistake,
  since it is a bit of a gotcha and really only exists for a niche
  optimization.
- Unused params, which could be fixed via '_'. There are hundreds of
  these in the code base and it is debatable if they should be fixed.
- Warnings about documentation, broadly ignored, since often they were
  related to having a '// TODO...' with no other documentation. Fixed
  examples that just needed moving text around instead of adding
  documentation
- Unhand-led errors, since these are often just being used in defer or
  from a printing statement, and wrapping them to be explicitly
  ignored is verbose
- Some examples of unused vars in tests, because they smelt of
  incomplete tests, i.e. there should have cases that used
  them.
- Some name collisions, especially with 'len' and 'delete', because
  they smelt of overly smart meta-programming going on, and I didn't
  feel like sussing out what was going on

commit.subject: Cherry pick "Revert "Handle vkGetPipelineCacheData() data size""
commit.message:
Cherry pick "Revert "Handle vkGetPipelineCacheData() data size""

Original change's description:
> Revert "Handle vkGetPipelineCacheData() data size"
> 
> This reverts commit 850fd541d4796ed41fdbd96374b995a49836ca93.
> 
> Reason for revert: Increase in crash rate when loading serialized
> data into VkPipelineCacheCreateInfo after landing.
> 
> Bug: 437807243
> Original change's description:
> > Handle vkGetPipelineCacheData() data size
> >
> > When PipelineCacheVk serializes VkPiplineCache it calls
> > vkGetPipelineCacheData() twice. The first call gets the size of the
> > data, then a blob of that size is allocated and the second call
> > serializes into the blob. While the size generally doesn't change
> > between the two calls it's technically possible.
> >
> > If the size written is smaller than the allocated blob then copy data to
> > a blob of right size (Blob has no truncate functionality). Also treat
> > VK_INCOMPLETE as success since valid bytes were written.
> >
> > Bug: 437807243

commit.subject: Change DAWN_BUILD_MONOLITHIC_LIBRARY default value.
commit.message:
Change DAWN_BUILD_MONOLITHIC_LIBRARY default value.

Update the default from `OFF` to `STATIC` such that, by default the
`libwebgpu*` files will be generated. The user can turn it to `OFF` if
they'd prefer to link against Dawn itself instead of webgpu.

This clears up some confusion by generating the webgpu libraries by
default.

Change-Id: Ifd81b0cb0ff9552e9576990f8e97d95bf96015ac

commit.subject: Allow objects to become error objects after initialization.
commit.message:
Allow objects to become error objects after initialization.

Objects that may do internal initialization or validation in
asynchronous tasks can now become error objects instead of needing to be
recreated.

Add another bit to the RefCounted payload to represent initialization
state. Checking the error state is only valid if the object has marked
itself as initialized. The values of error and initialization
enums allow atomic operations on the payload data to make the allowed
transitions.

No objects currently mark themselves as having delayed initialization.

Change-Id: Ied2bc6aae1b59f5c7c254a8db5e3ddabc11dfc4f

commit.subject: [setup-build] fix 'cmake install' scenario
commit.message:
[setup-build] fix 'cmake install' scenario

The 'install' option configures Dawn to be built
as a monolithic library, either as shared or static.
This is incompatible with BUILD_SHARED_LIBS.

Rearrange the logic so BUILD_SHARED_LIBS is only turned
on when *not* installing.

Signed-off-by: dneto <dneto@google.com>
Change-Id: I6a6a6964837e57a5a6a64da5c99878e1922bb127

commit.message:
Add ImmediateDataBufferLengthTests

and buffer length because they will shared
immediate block on all backends.

to ensure state management is correct.

commit.message:
Revert "Move FencedDeleter Tick into a SerialTask"

This reverts commit a3335349674d8e6538e35ae0f43ed84767b9f539.

Reason for revert: Most likely CL in regression range for https://crbug.com/443110641

Bug: 430452846
Original change's description:
> Move FencedDeleter Tick into a SerialTask
>
> Moves all of the deletions done by FencedDeleter into a SerialTask,
> rather than requiring that Tick be called manually. Tasks are scheduled
> when DeleteWhenUnused is called.
>
> To prevent an excessive amount of tasks from being created and to
> preserve deletion ordering for dependent resources (such as Swapchains
> and Surfaces) all deletions sharing a serial will share a task.
>

commit.subject: Move FencedDeleter Tick into a SerialTask
commit.message:
Move FencedDeleter Tick into a SerialTask

Moves all of the deletions done by FencedDeleter into a SerialTask,
rather than requiring that Tick be called manually. Tasks are scheduled
when DeleteWhenUnused is called.

To prevent an excessive amount of tasks from being created and to
preserve deletion ordering for dependent resources (such as Swapchains
and Surfaces) all deletions sharing a serial will share a task.

Bug: 430452846
Change-Id: Ie26bfad14087430f53e73f5c41a3897eb9f1e403

commit.message:
[dawn][native][d3d12] Remove dynamic allocation of limits in root signature

The root signature and the base limit sizes are the same on all D3D12
devices so there's no reason to allocate these dynamically, it just
makes it easier for one limit change to implicitly change other limits
(see bug).

Instead, choose constants for all of these limits and then just assert
that we've allocated them the way we expect.

commit.subject: [dawn] Ensure release bounds checks in ityp::*
commit.message:
[dawn] Ensure release bounds checks in ityp::*

Add death tests to ensure out-of-bounds accesses in all the ityp::*
containers crashes in release.

Both std (libc++) and absl are supposed to be configured to guarantee
this, so we don't need our own checks for those.

Fix ityp::array/vector/stack_vec by just removing the DAWN_ASSERT. That
was telling the compiler to assume its condition is true, causing it to
elide the bounds checks inside libc++ (that are supposed to always be
enabled for safety).

Fix ityp::span by changing the DAWN_ASSERT to a DAWN_CHECK. This should
really be changed to be based on std::span but that should be done
separately.

Bug: 442444724, 442860471
Change-Id: I7c37fc9c382b840a09df0b00dd782a5cdb80de6e

commit.subject: [tint] Add missing includes
commit.message:
[tint] Add missing includes

When Tint is built with only the SPIR-V reader and WGSL writer enabled
(e.g. because it's being used for SPIR-V to WGSL conversion and
nothing else), we need to explicitly include the ir::Module header.

We also need `tint::Program` when the WGSL writer is enabled, for the
program printer.

Change-Id: I47f0f48dd173c4f16bffb7e5a0548193ea62b634

commit.subject: Revert "Handle vkGetPipelineCacheData() data size"
commit.message:
Revert "Handle vkGetPipelineCacheData() data size"

This reverts commit 850fd541d4796ed41fdbd96374b995a49836ca93.

Reason for revert: Increase in crash rate when loading serialized
data into VkPipelineCacheCreateInfo after landing.

Bug: 437807243
Original change's description:
> Handle vkGetPipelineCacheData() data size
>
> When PipelineCacheVk serializes VkPiplineCache it calls
> vkGetPipelineCacheData() twice. The first call gets the size of the
> data, then a blob of that size is allocated and the second call
> serializes into the blob. While the size generally doesn't change
> between the two calls it's technically possible.
>
> If the size written is smaller than the allocated blob then copy data to
> a blob of right size (Blob has no truncate functionality). Also treat
> VK_INCOMPLETE as success since valid bytes were written.
>
> Bug: 437807243
> Change-Id: I4b2429dc22ae476b2d46e1024bcc6aebf10b0ace

commit.subject: Handle vkGetPipelineCacheData() data size
commit.message:
Handle vkGetPipelineCacheData() data size

When PipelineCacheVk serializes VkPiplineCache it calls
vkGetPipelineCacheData() twice. The first call gets the size of the
data, then a blob of that size is allocated and the second call
serializes into the blob. While the size generally doesn't change
between the two calls it's technically possible.

If the size written is smaller than the allocated blob then copy data to
a blob of right size (Blob has no truncate functionality). Also treat
VK_INCOMPLETE as success since valid bytes were wr437807243itten.

Bug: 437807243
Change-Id: I4b2429dc22ae476b2d46e1024bcc6aebf10b0ace

parents.subject: [dawn][metal] Adds spontaneous tests for queue events in Metal.

commit.subject: [dawn][wire] Adds capability to passthrough callback modes in wire.
commit.message:
[dawn][wire] Adds capability to passthrough callback modes in wire.

- Functionally, this change shouldn't do anything yet. It just adds
  a boolean argument when creating the wire server to allow for
  passing through callback modes via the wire. With the boolean set
  to true, this change should allow clients to specify spontaneous
  events such that when the native server side completes, it shows
  up on the client side spontaneously.

Change-Id: Ie86fddcaa587fe25c692a5a0cbde19cac0df8d58

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Update typeId metadata for dynamic binding arrays.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Update typeId metadata for dynamic binding arrays.

This metadata is used inside shader to know what to return for
hasBinding<T>(resource_binding, u/i32) for the various kinds of T.
This CL adds all the mechanisms to track and update the typeIds but only
makes the difference between "empty" and "texture_2d<f32>".

 - In Textures, add a map of all then (DynamicArrayState, slot) they are
   referenced in, and maintain it as DynamicArrayStates are created and
   destroyed. (this map contains WeakRefs to the DynamicArrayState to
   break what would otherwise be a ref cycle),
 - Add support for Hash to WeakRef for the above map.
 - Notify the DynamicArrayState on texture.Pin/Unpin so that it can
   track the "pinned" status of each slot.
 - In DynamicArrayState maintain the tint::ResourceType for each slot
   and return a list of updates to the metadata that backends must
   perform before using the dynamic binding array.
 - In the Vulkan backend, implement this update of the binding array
   metadata.
 - Fix an issue in Vulkan where setting a destroyed texture in the
   dynamic binding array at creation, would cause a VK_NULL_HANDLE to be
   written in vkWriteDescriptorSets, which is invalid.
 - Add a bunch of tests that hasBinding works correctly to exercise the
   newly added code paths.

Change-Id: Ie5a4568f033cb3f8d0d7dac29a9575514564a32e

commit.subject: [dawn][vk] Set up the metadata buffer for Tint's resource_binding.
commit.message:
[dawn][vk] Set up the metadata buffer for Tint's resource_binding.

Tint's support for `resource_binding` is done with a transform that
needs to know where the metadata buffer will be. Add that information in
the options set up in vulkan::ShaderModule.

Add tests that the metadata buffer is correctly set up by checking that
WGSL's arrayLength on `resource_binding` works correctly.

commit.subject: Tasks are synchronous after AssumeCommandsComplete
commit.message:
Tasks are synchronous after AssumeCommandsComplete

Ensures that once AssumeCommandsComplete has been called all future
tasks will be executed immediately rather than being placed on the
serial task queue. This prevents tasks scheduled during device teardown
fromt "leaking".

Bug: 430452846
Change-Id: I67ca6f5906cb001f89f6ca800ff290f9e9104f88

commit.message:
Validate a subtype exists before decoding a type.

In the IR decoder we may attempt to create a `TexelBuffer` ro
`StorageTexture` based on a given texel format. That format may not be
valid for creating the necessary subtype. Validate in the decoder before
attempting to create the type.

commit.message:
Stop ir decoder from attempting to create invalid arrays.

The array helpers expect the element type to exist. The IR fuzzer can
try to create arrays without element types. Check in the decoder and
return an invalid type if the element is a `nullptr`

parents.subject: Generate `getBinding` in SPIR-V.

commit.subject: Add a length check to `hasBinding`.
commit.message:
Add a length check to `hasBinding`.

When we do the `hasBinding` check make sure that we're within the array
size. If we're outside, we'll get robustness kicking in and give us a
value from the array which isn't what we want. So, verify we're within
the buffer size before trying to check the kind at the given index.

When we do the `hasBinding` check make sure that we're within the array
size. If we're outside, we'll get robustness kicking in and give us a
value from the array which isn't what we want. So, verify we're within
the buffer size before trying to check the kind at the given index.

commit.subject: Fix missing <cstdint> include in TypedInteger.h
commit.message:
Fix missing <cstdint> include in TypedInteger.h

I wasn't able to build Dawn on Ubuntu 25.04 w/ GCC 14.2.0 because of the following error:
```
In file included from /tmp/dawn-20250829.192131/src/dawn/common/ityp_array.h:36,
                 from /tmp/dawn-20250829.192131/out/Debug/gen/src/dawn/native/ObjectType_autogen.h:5,
                 from /tmp/dawn-20250829.192131/out/Debug/gen/src/dawn/native/ObjectType_autogen.cpp:2:
/tmp/dawn-20250829.192131/src/dawn/common/TypedInteger.h: In constructor ‘constexpr dawn::detail::TypedIntegerImpl<Tag, T>::TypedIntegerImpl(I)’:
/tmp/dawn-20250829.192131/src/dawn/common/TypedInteger.h:103:35: error: ‘uint64_t’ does not name a type
  103 |         static_assert(static_cast<uint64_t>(std::numeric_limits<I>::max()) <=
      |                                   ^~~~~~~~
/tmp/dawn-20250829.192131/src/dawn/common/TypedInteger.h:40:1: note: ‘uint64_t’ is defined in header ‘<cstdint>’; this is probably fixable by adding ‘#include <cstdint>’
```

Adding the missing include fixes the issue.

This is an imported pull request from
https://github.com/google/dawn/pull/44

commit.subject: Move VkCommandPool recycling to a SerialTask
commit.message:
Move VkCommandPool recycling to a SerialTask

Moves the recycling and resetting of VkCommandPools/CommandBuffers to
a SerialTask tracked on the Queue.

SerialTask processing is not handled on a separate thread yet, but that
is the plan of record. A couple changes were made in anticipation of
that point:
 1) mUnusedCommands was made MutexProtected.
 2) Resetting CommandPools was moved from the point that the recycled
    pool was retrieved to the task that recycles it.

This is also the first such task to be used by the Vulkan backend, and
as such the SerialTask queue needed to be pumped. Calls to
UpdateCompletedSerialTo were added to the Vulkan Queue
CheckAndUpdateCompletedSerials and DestroyImpl methods to facilitate it.

Bug: 430452846
Change-Id: I605b1086a53ee98b282dc1fd4a77985dbf2561a1

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Make WaitForIdle handle tasks up to pending serial.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Make WaitForIdle handle tasks up to pending serial.

- Adds assertions to ensure that we finish all tasks when the
  ExecutionQueue is destroyed.
- Instead of only completing tasks up to the completed serial in
  WaitForIdleForDestruction, complete tasks up to the pending serial.
  This is important because Dawn can end up scheduling tasks on the
  pending serial if the result of the task doesn't need to be
  observable to the user until the next commands are submitted. The
  example, and issue that we observed, was lazily clearing buffers
  that we call MapAsync on. See the comment in the code for more
  details.

Change-Id: I7c38e01c93548b273ffa553d28d32e38769644d8

commit.message:
[dawn][native] Split DynamicArrayState to its own class.

The logic of the dynamic array is very different from the one for static
bindings of a BindGroup. Tracking of pinned / unpinned resources and
metadata buffer updates will get non-trivial so it is better to separate
the classes in different files.

commit.subject: Fix an incorrect check in TypedIntegerImpl
commit.message:
Fix an incorrect check in TypedIntegerImpl

This patch fixes an incorrect check in the constructor of
`TypedIntegerImpl`. When `I` is a signed integer and `T` is
an unsigned integer, `std::numeric_limits<I>::min()` is negative
while `std::numeric_limits<T>::max()` is an unsigned value, so
`std::numeric_limits<I>::min()` will be implicitly converted to
an unsigned value, which is not expected. This will also cause a
`signed/unsigned integer mismatch` warning when we build Dawn with
clang.

In this patch we fix this issue by requiring `rhs` to be non-negative
and always convert `std::numeric_limits<T>::max()` and
`std::numeric_limits<I>::min()` to be uint64_t when `I` is a signed
integer and `T` is an unsigned integer.

Bug: 424536624
Change-Id: I7deed22a5ae1a5a13d0a39e46a812f6bbb2216ec

commit.subject: [dawn][vk] Implement Texture::Pin/Unpin.
commit.message:
[dawn][vk] Implement Texture::Pin/Unpin.

In the Vulkan backend, a pinned texture always stays in the same layout
(and must have all subresources initialized). This CL also adds
mechanisms and TODOs to ensure that backends always see balanced pin /
unpin pairs at it could duplicate logic if they had to sanitize
pin/unpin themselves.

In each backend, special care will be needed to find what needs to
happen when imported textures are pinned, because it might make fence
import/export a bit more tricky to handle. Added TODOs in the Vulkan
backend for this.

Finally some simple end2end tests of Pin/Unpin are added, which ensure
that sanitizing of Pin/Unpin happens in the frontend.

Bug: 435317394
Change-Id: Ib7d5d3d9a9a79748ee46b8968e0e5f0bc2c7ee52

commit.subject: Add invocationCreator bindings to non-shadow realms
commit.message:
Add invocationCreator bindings to non-shadow realms

Adds LUCI bindings for the role/resultdb.invocationCreator role to
relevant groups and service accounts in the non-shadow CI and try
realms.

This is necessary to properly run tests with ResultDB directly on
builders (instead of only through Swarming), as the builder will need to
create a ResultDB invocation for the local tests.

Bug: 441328362, 441327468
Change-Id: Ie0e86d6566a6f0488e4e5d2f34778df9c9bca065

commit.message:
Add gn_v2 fuzz builders

Adds dawn-linux-x64-builder-fuzz-rel, dawn-linux-x64-sws-fuzz-rel, and
their manual trybot equivalent. These currently do not build or test
anything, but they will eventually run the Dawn fuzz tests.

The CI builders are not currently triggered by the main poller since we
want to make sure they will be green before doing so.

Bug: 441327468

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Removes acquiring the device lock for many APIs.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Removes acquiring the device lock for many APIs.

- A lot of the APIs don't actually need the device lock. Originally,
  I think the intention was to try to remove the lock at a larger
  grain scope at a time instead of this case-by-case, but given that
  profiling and tracing has shown that the device lock contention
  can result in ~10% of performance time, this is an initial pass
  to comb through some likely hot places where the lock can be
  contention but unnecessary.

Bug: 422741977
Change-Id: I81fa51b20cb4d7bde34e975fc8762119e5c9151e

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Add Texture::Pin/Unpin frontend validation.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Add Texture::Pin/Unpin frontend validation.

The bindless extensions need a way to reduce the cost of memory barrier
tracking and usage scope validation. Usage pinning is the chosen method
for the prototyping in Dawn: it forces the texture to stay in a specific
usage until unpinned (or re-pinned). Backends no longer need to track
the texture as they can emit the necessary memory barrier when Pin() is
called.

Note that part of the validation for Pin() is missing because at submit
time we should check that all non-bindless usages of the texture are in
the pinned set of usages, but doing so could cause performance
regressions so it is skipped for now.

Bug: 435317394
Change-Id: Iaed7e5c77d35568ff8d3978d32f09ecad7f138c2

commit.subject: Run `gn format` directly.
commit.message:
Run `gn format` directly.

Currently the generation script runs the `gn.py` script through
depot_tools using `vpython3`. Instead. run the `gn` which is pulled in
through the DEPS file directly.

Note, this will only work on a linux, mac or windows machine as we only
pull `gn` for those versions. If we find we have developers on other
platforms, we may want to conditionalize this and fall back to the
python `gn.py` script to find `gn`.

This cuts about 4s off the gen time on my M3.

Change-Id: Ifc6201e8088bc9f65da573f633d8bf9574160bb8

commit.subject: Stop formatting generated cc and h files.
commit.message:
Stop formatting generated cc and h files.

Update the tint generator script to no longer call `clang-format` on any
generated `cc` or `h` file. Instead wrap those files in a `clang-format
off/on` pair so formatting will be skipped.

This saves about 7s on a run of `./tools/run gen` on my M3 Mac.

Change-Id: I7f7e16945b97b166d04b9505accdf49b9b25f691

commit.message:
[dawn][wire] Crash client when reusing objects from old wire

This does NOT give the correct behavior (which would be to produce a
"[object] cannot be used with [device]" validation error), but it does
prevent old client objects from misassociating with new server objects.

commit.subject: [dawn][wire] Crash client when reusing objects from old wire
commit.message:
[dawn][wire] Crash client when reusing objects from old wire

This is of course the incorrect behavior (we are supposed to produce a
"[object] cannot be used with [device]" validation error), but it does
prevent old client objects from misassociating with new server objects.
This avoids any possible security issue when that happens (though none
has been identified).

This crash can only happen after the GPU process has already crashed.
It's very hard to imagine this crash being hit in the wild by a
non-hostile application. It would require either having a bug where
objects from old devices are reused on a new device after recovery, or
having the application for some reason try to rely on push+popErrorScope
to check whether objects are from the same device. That would work fine
in most cases (e.g. device.destroy() which would be the typical way for
applications to test their recovery behavior), it would just not work in
cases where the GPU process has crashed.

Bug: 435630456
Change-Id: I73a2d816358bbfe9840cfecfe954c3d3c1b34bcf

parents.subject: Roll ANGLE from b98d052511a1 to 1c245d908ff3 (7 revisions)

commit.subject: vulkan: Use host cached memory for read buffers
commit.message:
vulkan: Use host cached memory for read buffers

Investigation in https://crbug.com/432691010 found that memcpy() reading
data from a read only transfer buffer was ~10x slower with
Graphite/Dawn/Vulkan when compared to Ganesh/Vulkan. This was identified
as being caused by dawn using host coherent memory instead of host
cached.

Switch BufferVK to use host cached memory for read only transfer
buffers, aka those created with only BufferUsage::MapRead|Copydst, to
avoid this hangup. BufferVk also has to make explicit flush and
invalidate calls for non-host coherent memory.

Bug: 432691010
Change-Id: I723f19a75e67fff5b2e45e9bac20b9e948fd3014

commit.message:
[dawn][native] Require BGL dynamic array even for size 0 BG dynamic array

Allowing BG dynamic arrays of size 0 on BGLs without dynamic arrays
turned out to cause a few issues, disallow it for now and revisit later
depending on what the spec / webgpu.h decides.

commit.message:
[dawn][native] Require BGL dynamic array even for size 0 BG dynamic array

Prior to this CL, a special case in the validation allowed a BG with a
dynamic array size of 0 to be compatible with a BGL without a dynamic
array. This turned out to cause a few issues. Disallow it for now and
revisit later depending on what the spec / webgpu.h decides.

commit.message:
[dawn][native] Require BGL dynamic array even for size 0 BG dynamic array

Prior to this CL, a special case in the validation allowed a BG with a
dynamic array size of 0 to be compatible with a BGL without a dynamic
array. This turned out to cause a few issues. Disallow it for now and
revisit later depending on what the spec / webgpu.h decides.

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Add BindGroup::Destroy(), only for dynamic binding arrays
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Add BindGroup::Destroy(), only for dynamic binding arrays

Dynamic binding arrays may contain an arbitrary amount of data. Add a
.destroy() method like for other container objects, except that it is
only allowed if the BindGroup has a dynamic array.

Add tests for this, and since the tests no longer test the creation of
BindGroup/Layout, add bindless MakeBindGroup/Layout utilities for use in
these new tests.

commit.subject: [dawn][vk] Implement dynamic array BindGroup creation.
commit.message:
[dawn][vk] Implement dynamic array BindGroup creation.

 - Add a second vkUpdateDescriptorSets call in
   vulkan::BindGroup::InitializeImpl that populates the dynamic array
   part. (and split InitializeImpl in two)
 - Add getters in BindGroupBase to query the dynamic array information.
   The tracking is split in its own DynamicArrayState structure as it
   is expected to grow a lot and can be a separate allocation to avoid
   bloating BindGroup.
 - In BindGroupBase::Initialize, populate the DynamicArrayState with the
   bindings that are in the dynamic array (if any).
 - Add a utility method on BindGroupLayout to convert a BindingNumber to
   a BindingIndex that's the index in the dynamic array.
 - Add a few end2end tests for the creation and destruction of dynamic
   array BindGroups. These with the VVLs caught 4 different issues (and
   found one Swiftshader bug).

commit.subject: [dawn][vk] Implement dynamic array BindGroup creation.
commit.message:
[dawn][vk] Implement dynamic array BindGroup creation.

 - Add a second vkUpdateDescriptorSets call in
   vulkan::BindGroup::InitializeImpl that populates the dynamic array
   part. (and split InitializeImpl in two)
 - Add getters in BindGroupBase to query the dynamic array information.
   The tracking is split in its own DynamicArrayState structure as it
   is expected to grow a lot and can be a separate allocation to avoid
   bloating BindGroup.
 - In BindGroupBase::Initialize, populate the DynamicArrayState with the
   bindings that are in the dynamic array (if any).
 - Add a utility method on BindGroupLayout to convert a BindingNumber to
   a BindingIndex that's the index in the dynamic array.
 - Add a few end2end tests for the creation and destruction of dynamic
   array BindGroups. These with the VVLs caught 4 different issues (and
   found one Swiftshader bug).

commit.subject: Capture: Emit Shared RenderBundle Commands
commit.message:
Capture: Emit Shared RenderBundle Commands

Note: I separated out these commands into
EncodeRenderBundleCommand because that is what other
backends do but that separation is no needed here.
A render bundle in WGPU should end up making a backend
render bunndle (an mInnerHandle to a MTL/VK/D3D render bundle).
But, that's not currently how dawn appears to work.

We probably need to playback the WGPU render bundle
commands into an inner render bundle when the bundle
encoder is ended to generate an inner render bundle.

Still, this code should work for playing back
render pass commands. We can refactor later
if we want to use for the case above.

commit.message:
Add iOS and Android prebuilt binaries to the CI

The goal of this PR is to provide iOS and Android prebuilt binaries. These are the ones we use in React Native WebGPU.
For iOS, we apply a tiny patch to build a static lib file instead of a dynamic lib file because React Native still uses CocoaPods and we need to have a fat lib file with all architectures inside.

commit.subject: [dawn][native][d3d12] Force higher minimums for maxDynamic* limits
commit.message:
[dawn][native][d3d12] Force higher minimums for maxDynamic* limits

Adding maxImmediateSize to D3D12 took space away from
maxDynamicUniformBuffersPerPipelineLayout and
maxDynamicStorageBuffersPerPipelineLayout, which is a regression.
Set those first, so that allocating maxImmediateSize can't take away
from them.

This should be safe for all machines because kMaxRootSignatureSize and
the default values for the limits are all constants, so all this
allocation logic has the same logic on all machines.

commit.subject: [ir] Tighten check for non-constructible types
commit.message:
[ir] Tighten check for non-constructible types

Instead of allowing all non-constructible types when the
pointer-and-handles-in-structs capability is enabled, only allow
non-constructible structures.

This prevents other non-constructible types, such as `void`, being
incorrectly allowed.

Fixed: 441041287
Change-Id: Ic4134713ce661b63326be436297a5e01446dfb90

commit.subject: [dawn][d3d12] Force higher minimums for maxDynamic* limits
commit.message:
[dawn][d3d12] Force higher minimums for maxDynamic* limits

Adding maxImmediateSize to D3D12 took space away from
maxDynamicUniformBuffersPerPipelineLayout and
maxDynamicStorageBuffersPerPipelineLayout, which is a regression.
Set those first, so that allocating maxImmediateSize can't take away
from them.

This should be safe for all machines because kMaxRootSignatureSize and
the default values for the limits are all constants, so all this
allocation logic has the same logic on all machines.

Fixed: 440381283
Change-Id: I679481bf6a31cda73c117d5b7c9518b59f9008b6

Remove chromium-experimental-primitive-id

Now that Dawn has been updated to use the primitive-index feature
name, the previous chromium-experimental-primitive-id enum can be
removed.

temporarily to avoid accidentally shipping the feature before we
get approval on the Intent to Ship.

commit.subject: [msl] Avoid adding new functions while iterating over them
commit.message:
[msl] Avoid adding new functions while iterating over them

Updating usages of function parameters in the PackedVec3 transform can
introduce new helper functions, so we need to take a copy of the
function list before we start iterating over it.

Fixed: 440127431
Change-Id: Iefab3c1536548571c59392c8fc2d5f17477809ce

commit.subject: Add the wire client version of webgpu_cpp_print.h
commit.message:
Add the wire client version of webgpu_cpp_print.h

This CL adds the generation of webgpu_cpp_print.h for wire client
(under the include/dawn/wire/client path). Currently some places in
Chromium (e.g. webgpu_test) that should use the wire client types are
actually using the native headers instead. However, with the addition
of ClientSharedImage and WebGPUTextureScopedAccess, the correct header
usage is now mandatory. This change serves as a prerequisite for the
header refactoring on the Chromium side.

Bug: 439767645, 40286368
Change-Id: I4f4a4afdcb35b6e5089e31c450a4c523f98024d6

[spirv-reader] Fix issue with switch in switch default.

If the default block of a switch had a switch in it then we'd move the
current switch blocks pointer out from under ourselves. Use an index
instead of a reference.

commit.subject: [dawn][vk] Implement dynamic array BGLs
commit.message:
[dawn][vk] Implement dynamic array BGLs

In Vulkan the equivalent concept to dynamic binding arrays are
descriptor arrays with all the VK_KHR_descriptor_indexing flags
enabled. The allocation strategy for the VkDescriptorSet needs to change
as the sets may have varying size even if used on the same layout. This
in turns requires a different, simpler version of the
DescriptorSetAllocator to be used.

In order to minimize the amount of additional branching that happens
because of the bindless path (which is cold, but static-only bindgroups
are perf critical), BindGroupLayoutVk is split into two subclasses that
dispatch to the regular DescriptorSetAllocator or a new
DescriptorSetAllocatorDynamicArray. (I tried 4 different approaches and
the current one seems to be the less disgusting one)

Changes in this CL are:

 - Remove logic in DescriptorSetAllocator to handle pool sizes of 0 as
   this is no longer a Vulkan error to do, and VVLs don't complain
   anymore.
 - Add DescriptorSetAllocatorDynamicArray that creates descriptor sets
   with variable counts and doesn't do any recycling or suballocation of
   the underlying VkDescriptorPool (apps should create few dynamic array
   bindgroups).
 - Split vulkan::BindGroupLayout into a base class and a child class for
   StaticBindingOnly.
 - Factor out the code that computes information related to static
   bindings into its own function.
 - Add a BindGroupLayoutDynamicArray that creates a
   VkDescriptorSetLayout with a variable count and uses
   DescriptorSetAllocatorDynamicArray.
 - In BindGroupLayoutInternalBase, decide that the dynamic array will
   directly follow the static bindings, and have separate getters that
   return either a BindingNumber or a BindingIndex.

This change can barely be tested on its own, but end2end tests with
BindGroup dynamic array creation in follow up CLs found a bunch of bugs
and will provide coverage.

Bug: 439522242
Change-Id: Ia24227aed66831caa4cb8d3bfe1407ed420fdca2

commit.subject: [dawn][vk] Implement dynamic array BGLs
commit.message:
[dawn][vk] Implement dynamic array BGLs

In Vulkan the equivalent concept to dynamic binding arrays are
descriptor arrays with all the VK_KHR_descriptor_indexing flags
enabled. The allocation strategy for the VkDescriptorSet needs to change
as the sets may have varying size even if used on the same layout. This
in turns requires a different, simpler version of the
DescriptorSetAllocator to be used.

In order to minimize the amount of additional branching that happens
because of the bindless path (which is cold, but static-only bindgroups
are perf critical), BindGroupLayoutVk is split into two subclasses that
dispatch to the regular DescriptorSetAllocator or a new
DescriptorSetAllocatorDynamicArray. (I tried 4 different approaches and
the current one seems to be the less disgusting one)

Changes in this CL are:

 - Remove logic in DescriptorSetAllocator to handle pool sizes of 0 as
   this is no longer a Vulkan error to do, and VVLs don't complain
   anymore.
 - Add DescriptorSetAllocatorDynamicArray that creates descriptor sets
   with variable counts and doesn't do any recycling or suballocation of
   the underlying VkDescriptorPool (apps should create few dynamic array
   bindgroups).
 - Split vulkan::BindGroupLayout into a base class and a child class for
   StaticBindingOnly.
 - Factor out the code that computes information related to static
   bindings into its own function.
 - Add a BindGroupLayoutDynamicArray that creates a
   VkDescriptorSetLayout with a variable count and uses
   DescriptorSetAllocatorDynamicArray.
 - In BindGroupLayoutInternalBase, decide that the dynamic array will
   directly follow the static bindings, and have separate getters that
   return either a BindingNumber or a BindingIndex.

This change can barely be tested on its own, but end2end tests with
BindGroup dynamic array creation in follow up CLs found a bunch of bugs
and will provide coverage.

commit.message:
[dawn][native] Reverts a change that's causing memory leak on fuzzer.

- In https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/251875 I added
  an additional reference to the queue that is held by the serial
  tasks, but it turns out that it's actually not needed and
  problematic because it can cause a reference cycle leading to
  leakage. Reverts the change and updates the comment.

Bug: 440369555, 440158604
Change-Id: I2fb39cd219ee491150228c9ec34e98a8e5c1082c

commit.subject: Disable use_libcxx_modules for the transitive rdeps of common_config.
commit.message:
Disable use_libcxx_modules for the transitive rdeps of common_config.

The dxc_module template defines common_config in `public_configs`. This means that anything that transitively depends on :common_config cannot use libcxx_modules.

It is currently configured to compile the libraries correctly, but cannot compile the executable targets that depend on them correctly.

Bug: 425537956
Change-Id: If2d1ad66a100c02af6be0f785b051f0bfe1497d2

[wgsl] Minify whitespace

When minification is enabled, strip all unnecessary whitespace from
generated WGSL. The only whitespace that needs to be preserved is
between two tokens that are identifier-like tokens (e.g. user
identifiers, keywords, enums, etc).

commit.subject: [wgsl] Move helper functions that check for WGSL special words
commit.message:
[wgsl] Move helper functions that check for WGSL special words

This allows them to also be used by other components, such as the WGSL
minification logic.

Also change the enum and type helpers to use the enum parsing logic,
which makes them more robust to future additions to these enums (for
example "immediate" was not covered yet).

Bug: 438518200
Change-Id: Ic7afc70a0ba3246f26a430e1f8aff00c6e5c41f2

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Fixes device lock and queue lock inversion issues.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Fixes device lock and queue lock inversion issues.

- This change updates the ExecutionQueue to use an explicit mutex and
  condition variable to handle calling callbacks instead of using the
  simpler MutexProtected. This is necessary because we want to make
  sure that we never cause a lock inversion between the device lock
  and the queue lock as a result of calling into a re-entrant callback.
  By using the explicit mutex and condition variable, we can still
  enforce callback ordering without holding the queue lock while
  calling callbacks.

Bug: 436827639, 430401631, 412761228
Include-Ci-Only-Tests: true

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Fixes device lock and queue lock inversion issues.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Fixes device lock and queue lock inversion issues.

- This change updates the ExecutionQueue to use an explicit mutex and
  condition variable to handle calling callbacks instead of using the
  simpler MutexProtected. This is necessary because we want to make
  sure that we never cause a lock inversion between the device lock
  and the queue lock as a result of calling into a re-entrant callback.
  By using the explicit mutex and condition variable, we can still
  enforce callback ordering without holding the queue lock while
  calling callbacks.

Bug: 436827639, 430401631, 412761228
Include-Ci-Only-Tests: true
Change-Id: I96e986decb16b6f8c6986bf9119d938b6319fe1a

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Removes ExecutionQueue::CheckPassedSerials.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Removes ExecutionQueue::CheckPassedSerials.

- Updates EventManager to defer callbacks in the tasks. This scopes
  the defer so that only the callbacks are called without the
  device lock instead of trying to avoid holding the device lock
  for more pieces of the code.
- Moves the UpdateCompletedSerial back into the critical section
  in the EventManager to avoid the bug listed below. This is also
  possible now because the task will defer the callback until the
  lock is released.
- Removes the outdated CheckPassedSerials calls and use
  UpdateCompletedSerial instead.
- Updates CheckPassedSerials to use the result of the FetchMax
  instead of the passed argument. This should make it possible
  for races to processes more than before and have less contention.

Bug: 430401631
Change-Id: I2a0b04287789f42157b44cd48d99d0d988171799

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Refactors ExecutionQueue to be an ApiObject.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Refactors ExecutionQueue to be an ApiObject.

- For a while I was avoiding changing the class heirachy to try to
  keep the ExecutionQueue separate from the Device, but with the
  locking issues, it was too hard to keep it separate and by
  changing it, it becomes a lot easier to manage the callbacks and
  ensure that we take the device lock in places to ensure that we
  don't ever run into lock inversion issues.
- Renames virtual WaitForQueueSerial->WaitForQueueSerialImpl to
  move logic into the ExecutionQueue instead of having the logic
  in the EventManager.
- In the ExecutionQueue, anytime we need to take the lock to
  |mWaitingTasks|, we now also take the device lock first. This
  was often the area where the lock inversion happens, so by
  forcing us to take the device lock first now, we should be able
  to avoid the whole class of issues. Note that this is made
  possible because the device lock is recursive now so re-entrant
  callbacks should still work fine.
- Removes the outdated CheckPassedSerials calls and use
  UpdateCompletedSerial instead. This means that Tick should now
  make forward progress on serial tasks.
- Updates CheckPassedSerials to use the result of the FetchMax
  instead of the passed argument. This should make it possible
  for races to processes more than before and have less contention.

Bug: 430401631
Include-Ci-Only-Tests: true
Change-Id: I2a0b04287789f42157b44cd48d99d0d988171799

commit.message:
[dawn][native] Refactors ExecutionQueue to be an ApiObject.

- For a while I was avoiding changing the class heirachy to try to
  keep the ExecutionQueue separate from the Device, but with the
  locking issues, it was too hard to keep it separate and by
  changing it, it becomes a lot easier to manage the callbacks and
  ensure that we take the device lock in places to ensure that we
  don't ever run into lock inversion issues.
- Renames virtual WaitForQueueSerial->WaitForQueueSerialImpl to
  move logic into the ExecutionQueue instead of having the logic
  in the EventManager. Also makes it return the serial that was
  completed so that we can update accordingly.
- In the ExecutionQueue, anytime we need to take the lock to
  |mWaitingTasks|, we now also take the device lock first. This
  was often the area where the lock inversion happens, so by
  forcing us to take the device lock first now, we should be able

  instead of the passed argument. This should make it possible
  for races to processes more than before and have less contention.
- Since the device wide lock is now required as a part of task
  updating in the ExecutionQueue, all the wait for functions now
  require that the device lock is NOT held. This is important
  because otherwise, the device lock will be held by the wait which
  sleeps without releasing the lock, thereby preventing any other
  threads from making forward progress when trying to acquire the
  device lock.

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Refactors ExecutionQueue to be an ApiObject.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Refactors ExecutionQueue to be an ApiObject.

- For a while I was avoiding changing the class hierarchy to try to
  keep the ExecutionQueue separate from the Device, but with the
  locking issues, it was too hard to keep it separate and by
  changing it, it becomes a lot easier to manage the callbacks and
  ensure that we take the device lock in places to ensure that we
  don't ever run into lock inversion issues. This also lets us
  introduce a toggle so that we can incrementally implement thread
  safety across different backends.
- Using the new toggle, we revert some of the changes from
  https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/252918 for backends
  other than Metal. We also update the implementation so that
  device.Destroy and error handling code takes the lock depending
  on the new toggle.
- In the ExecutionQueue, anytime we need to take the lock to
  |mWaitingTasks|, we now also take the device lock first. This
  was often the area where the lock inversion happens, so by
  forcing us to take the device lock first now, we should be able
  to avoid the whole class of issues. Note that this is made
  possible because the device lock is recursive now so re-entrant
  callbacks should still work fine.
- Move updating of serials into the lock so that inserting and
  running of callbacks are guaranteed.

Bug: 430401631, 412761228
Include-Ci-Only-Tests: true
Change-Id: I2a0b04287789f42157b44cd48d99d0d988171799

commit.subject: [spirv-reader][ir] Fix accessing struct members with row_major
commit.message:
[spirv-reader][ir] Fix accessing struct members with row_major

When accessing a struct with a row_major matrix, we incorrectly bailed
out if we didn't find the matrix in the access chain, but if the `var`
is an operand, we'll process the access for all struct members, so early
return in this case as we don't need to change anything.

Fixed: 439778566
Change-Id: Iebb44db99541ec41f982f1d6cd65ad33eab59103

commit.subject: D3D: Add d3d_skip_shader_optimizations toggle
commit.message:
D3D: Add d3d_skip_shader_optimizations toggle

Adds a new toggle, `d3d_skip_shader_optimizations`, to force the
D3DCOMPILE_SKIP_OPTIMIZATION flag during shader compilation in D3D11
and D3D12. This can be used to speed up shader compilation time by
skipping optimization passes.

Bug: 439845637
Change-Id: Ie085076b5c2e66b196d812fbb9cc3c6686b75923

commit.subject: [dawn][vk] Add missing StreamImpl for newly used structure.
commit.message:
[dawn][vk] Add missing StreamImpl for newly used structure.

The Vulkan backend serializes whole descriptors as cache keys. In the
previous CL adding support for VK_KHR_pipeline_robustness, the
CreateInfo was serialized before the chaining of the
VkPipelineRobustnessCreateInfo, which is incorrect.

Fix the ordering and add the missing StreamImpl<VkPipelineRobustnessCreateInfo>.

Bug: 439522242
Change-Id: Iaa808ce4c60dc289d5ef3f756fc2876a86303646

commit.message:
Kotlin: supply a hashCode on objects, matching the existing toEquals

Per `api_lint.ignore`, and more:

```
EqualsAndHashCode: androidx.webgpu.Adapter#equals(Object):
   Must override both equals and hashCode; missing one in androidx.webgpu.Adapter
```

The handle (Long) uniquely identifies the underlying object, so we can take the Int hash of that.

commit.subject: [dawn][vk] Handle robustBufferAccessUpdateAfterBind.
commit.message:
[dawn][vk] Handle robustBufferAccessUpdateAfterBind.

When this property is false, all forms of buffer robustness are
disallowed, except pipelineRobustness's vertexInputs robustness.

This CL adds:

 - Detection of the VK_EXT_pipeline_robustness extension (promoted to
   Vulkan 1.4).
 - Gates bindless on robustBufferAccessUpdateAfterBind or
   pipelineRobustness being present.
 - Adds logic to disable robustness on buffers (and not rely on it) when
   bindless is enabled and robustBufferAccessUpdateAfterBind is false.
 - Adds logic to request when creating a pipeline that robust access
   still happen on vertexInputs.

Alltogether this changes aim at supporting bindless anywhere we can
enable robustness on vertex inputs (because we don't want to emulate
that if we can avoid it), while taking advantage of as much of the
driver's robustness support as possible (like we currently do).

Bug: 435251399
Change-Id: I2164e3396bcbdc2f4c215ffe1568147c2d6aa062

commit.subject: Refactor ProgressBar for easier testing
commit.message:
Refactor ProgressBar for easier testing

Refactors ProgressBar to be an interface with two implementations,
RealProgressBar (the existing impl) & StubProgressBar (no-op for
unsupported terminals and testing.

The terminal character check is moved into the constructor to allow
selecting whether to return a RealProgressBar or a
StubProgressBar. Callers no longer need to perform the check
themselves, and are guaranteed to get a ProgressBar back, so can avoid
later nil checks.

This change bypasses the need to write a dependency injection wrapper
for the `term` package for testing fuzz/main.go

Bug: 344014313
Change-Id: I8e4d5342ce4f42750b3179730a72ab6a4c7ace1d

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Allow directly iterating over bindings of one type.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Allow directly iterating over bindings of one type.

The BindGroupLayout reorders bindings and sorts them by type. This means
that all buffers have a contiguous range, same for all textures,
samplers, etc. Code looking at BGLs can use this to directly iterate
over the bindings they are interested in instead of looping over
bindings and calling MatchVariant or std::get_if.

Introduce the scaffolding to support this kind of iteration and use it
to make more robust the places in the code that already assumed that
buffers are at the start.

Bug: 439565641
Change-Id: I235f6df8ee2f0a3dc3a86ac715b47d0f9028b31c

commit.message:
[dawn][vk] Freshen up comments in vulkan::{BGL, DescriptorSetAllocator}

These were outdated, had TODOs with too few details and associated with
people instead of issues, etc.

Also makes `DescriptorSetAllocator` a `RefCounted` as it doesn't need to
be `ObjectBase` with the error monad mechanism.

Also pass in the VkDescriptorSetLayout instead of the BindGroupLayout to
DescriptorSetAllocator::Allocate to make it more clear exactly what will
be used.

commit.subject: Add more Qualcomm compute device ids
commit.message:
Add more Qualcomm compute device ids

Only 8380 (0x363343xx) is derived from A7xx, while all the earlier
compute GPUs are based on A6xx.
A summarization of QC compute GPUs can be found at https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1wybODaXljgkhsBKadHtOWsGpVbIk7vR48B9-Rqsn_JY/edit?gid=0#gid=0

Please note Qualcomm_ACPI is used for D3D12 (compute), while Qualcomm_PCI (phone and compute) is used for Vulkan. In theory, all the devices in Qualcomm_ACPI should also be part of Qualcomm_PCI as they may run on Vulkan, and both masks should be 0xFFFFFF00. Currently I don't have enough detailed info about phone, so this CL leaves out the changes to Qualcomm_PCI.

Change-Id: I5f37c88c8e36c4388e01b2f2d47499cffebb7817

commit.subject: [tint][cmake] Use build protoc instead of system installed version
commit.message:
[tint][cmake] Use build protoc instead of system installed version

The existing cmake rule will use the first protoc that shows up in
your path, so will likely default to the system installed version of
protoc, which may not be compatible with the version of libprotobuf in
our repo. Additionally this can lead to build failures when there is
no installed protoc, and the output path for the build is not in the
path.

This also include a small fix for '"--${ARGS_LANGUAGE}_out', since
protoc uses '--<flag>=<arg>' or '-<flag><arg>' format for its CLI, not
'--<flag> <arg>'.

Fixes: 435357782
Change-Id: I20c921599caf5ac4b5c57545fb61886463092a13
